Loquacious

loh-KWAY-shus · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Loquacious is tending to talk a great deal, in a fluent and confident way.

The loquacious podcast host could turn a single question into a fascinating twenty-minute answer.

Worked Example

Even the shyest guests on her show became loquacious once she asked about their childhood pets.

Loquacious emphasizes fluent, confident, often skillful talkativeness -- a more even-handed or even admiring quality than garrulous.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

voluble: talking easily and at length

talkative: inclined to talk a great deal

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

taciturn: reluctant to speak much

laconic: using very few words

Where it sits · how smoothly the speech flows — talkative → loquacious → garrulous

talkative vs. loquacious: Talkative is the everyday, plain word; loquacious adds a sense of fluent, confident skill in speaking.

garrulous vs. loquacious: Garrulous pushes further than loquacious, adding a rambling, wearisome quality that loquacious doesn't necessarily carry.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — loqu

root — loqu: to speak (Latin (loqui))

suffix — -acious

suffix — -acious: full of, inclined to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: loqu- ('to speak') + -acious ('full of, inclined to') together mean 'full of speaking' -- fluently talkative.

Use the root in a new word: eloquent

Use the root in a new word: eloquent: Eloquent shares the same Latin root loqui ('to speak'), joined here with the prefix ex- ('out').
